headline.purpose: Page titles — one per screen, top of the content column.

body.purpose: Default text, table cells, form values.

label.purpose: Column headers, stat labels, sidebar section labels — always muted, uppercase.

numeric.purpose: Stat card values — one of the system's few large, load-bearing figures.

title-sm.purpose: Card titles — one step down from Title.

numeric-lg.purpose: The Business Volume entry field alone — the single largest text in the system.

caption.purpose: Secondary explanatory text quieter than a Label — card subtitles, bar-chart row labels/counts, the structure legend, small inline notes.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Modals, toasts, and the search-results dropdown.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: The one other shadow in the system — the active segment of a segmented control, a 1px tactile lift standing in for a color-fill affordance it doesn't have.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.purpose: Buttons, inputs, nav items, pin dots — fast, functional state changes, not decorative easing.

motion.name: overlay-in
motion.purpose: Modal/toast entrance (0.12–0.16s) — a small settle, not a bounce.

motion.name: bar-fill
motion.purpose: Slab-distribution bar width transitions on data change.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one call-to-action color per screen — save, confirm, add member.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 13px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid transparent; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 550; cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 0.1s, border-color 0.1s, opacity 0.1s; } .ds-btn-primary { background: #4f46e5; color: #fff; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4f46e5; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 13px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 550; cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 0.1s, border-color 0.1s; } .ds-btn-secondary { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; color: #0f172a; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #f8fafc; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4f46e5; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Pill — Active
components.description: Color always paired with a text label — never color alone.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; height: 21px; padding: 0 9px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 650; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-pill::before { content: ""; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-pill-active { background: #ecfdf5; color: #059669; } .ds-pill-active::before { background: #059669; }

components.name: Status Pill — Inactive
components.description: The inactive-member marker — display-only, no calculation effect, but always visible wherever a member row appears.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; height: 21px; padding: 0 9px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 650; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-pill::before { content: ""; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-pill-inactive { background: #fef2f2; color: #dc2626; } .ds-pill-inactive::before { background: #dc2626; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: The system's single field style — used identically for search, entry amounts, and every form input.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Search by name or 6-digit member number">
components.css: .ds-input { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0 11px; height: 34px; width: 100%; color: #0f172a; font-size: 14px; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #4f46e5; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #eef2ff; } .ds-input.ds-invalid { border-color: #dc2626; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat by default — border does the separation work, never a shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 8px; padding: 18px; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 650; margin-bottom: 2px; color: #0f172a; } .ds-card-sub { font-size: 12px; color: #64748b; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: The active item's indigo-weak fill is the single strongest 'you are here' signal in the system.
components.html: <button class="ds-nav-item ds-active"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" width="16" height="16"><path d="M3 11l9-8 9 8"/><path d="M5 10v10h14V10"/></svg>Home</button>
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 7px 10px; border-radius: 6px; color: #0f172a; font-size: 13.5px; cursor: pointer; border: none; background: none; width: 100%; text-align: left; } .ds-nav-item svg { flex-shrink: 0; opacity: 0.75; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #f8fafc; } .ds-nav-item.ds-active { background: #eef2ff; color: #4f46e5; font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-item.ds-active svg { opacity: 1; }

narrative.overview:
This is a private operating console for one person, read like a ledger every day: dense, numeric, and built to be trusted at a glance rather than admired. There is exactly one accent color and it is spent carefully — on the action that matters (primary buttons), the place the operator currently is (active nav), and the thing that just gained focus (inputs, rings) — never as decoration. Everything else lives in a tight range of slate neutrals against a near-white page.

The system is flat by design. Surfaces sit directly on the page with a 1px hairline border, not a shadow — depth is reserved for the handful of things that genuinely float above the page (a modal, a toast, a search-results dropdown). Status is never color alone: an inactive member gets a labelled pill, not a colored dot, because the one operator here is not asked to rely on color perception to run their business.

Numbers are the product. Every figure — a Business Volume entry, a team total, a stat card — is tabular and right-aligned so columns line up the way a real ledger's would; six-digit member numbers additionally take a monospace face so they read as fixed-width codes, distinct from prose. Nothing here uses the vocabulary of a commercial platform — the visible word list is closed (member, Business Volume, Rewards, royalty, volume, slab, level, leg) and that restraint extends to the visual language too: no gradients, no marketing hero type, no rounded-SaaS softness.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (indigo), spent sparingly, never decoratively
Flat by default; shadows only on things that float (modal, toast, search dropdown)
Status is a labelled pill, never a color alone
Every number is tabular; identifiers are monospace
Dense, ~40px table rows, restrained 6-8px radius, no ornament

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Indigo is the only brand color in the system. There is no secondary or tertiary accent — a second color need is solved with a status color or a neutral, never a new hue.

rules.name: The Color-Plus-Label Rule
rules.body: No status is ever conveyed by color alone. Active/Inactive, locked/unlocked, and every pill in the system pairs its color with a text label — this is a hard requirement (§11.8 accessibility, M4.5/M6.5), not a preference.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that could sit in a column — table cells, stat values, entered figures — uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Digits must line up; this system is read as a ledger, not prose.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only on something that overlays the page and will disappear again (modal, toast, dropdown) — never on a card, row, or anything that's part of the page's permanent layout.

rules.name: The Blended Alert Border Rule
rules.body: Warning and danger callouts don't use a pure status-colored border or a plain neutral one — they blend the status color 35% into the neutral border (color-mix(in srgb, var(--warning) 35%, var(--border))), softer than a solid alert color but still legible as one.

dos: Do keep the accent to one hue (Indigo) system-wide; solve a second-color need with a status color or a neutral.
Do pair every status color with a text label — pills, banners, and inactive-member rows are never color-only.
Do use tabular numerals for every figure that could sit in a column, and monospace specifically for member ID numbers.
Do keep the outstanding-month banner undismissable — no close icon, no auto-hide, ever (Rule 20).
Do stay inside the restricted vocabulary (member, Business Volume, Rewards, royalty, volume, slab, level, leg) in every visible string, including placeholder/empty-state copy and error messages.
Do reserve shadow for things that float temporarily above the page (modal, toast, search dropdown), plus the one narrow control-lift exception on a segmented control's active state.
Do gate any view that renders an unbounded number of nodes at once behind an explicit confirmation past a readable threshold — scrollable is not the same as readable.
donts: Don't add a shadow to a card, table row, or sidebar — flat-by-default is load-bearing to this system's density, not a stylistic default that can flex.
Don't introduce a second accent color, a gradient, or decorative color anywhere — this is a discreet, non-commercial tool by explicit client requirement, not a marketing surface.
Don't use commercial/MLM vocabulary (sale, purchase, order, cash, payment, commission, invoice) anywhere, including in mock or placeholder data.
Don't invent a new radius value outside the documented tiers (3px tiny marks, 6px controls, 8px containers, 10-14px large icon containers by formula, 999px fully round).
Don't let a structure-tree connector line take on the accent color or grow thicker than the node borders it connects — the diagram's data must always outweigh its scaffolding.
